analysis: The PR is documentation-only in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one row at head line 1741 to the daemon environment passthrough table: `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED`, which points to `GatedDeltaPrefill.mode` in libs/mlx-swift-lm and says `0` keeps the stock Qwen GDN prompt kernel. I examined this row against the supplied base text (units 4-6) and the threat model. The row documents a performance or kernel-selection toggle for the Qwen gated-delta prompt path. It does not touch coordinator authorization, attestation, App Attest, key custody, encryption, prefix-cache storage (T-041), the fan helper or the WebSocket contract. The cited source file is not supplied, so I cannot verify that the variable is actually forwarded by LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys, or that the 0/default semantics are correct. The sentence before the table says the table lists only variables copied into the plist. Any mismatch would be doc drift, not a security regression. The other threat-model concern is that a user-set env var could switch the prompt kernel to an unqualified numerical path. That would affect output correctness (T-007/T-056 class), and only the operator, who is already the adversary in TB-003, controls it. It grants no new capability, so I report no finding. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the unseen implementation: whether the kernel variants are numerically equivalent, and whether the toggle is read process-wide in a way that touches qualification or attestation claims. That is minor and not reviewable from this patch.
